The approximate Pareto front (non-dominated in modulus × pore fraction):
- **14-0add-8deg**: 103.6 bar, 0.75 — highest pore fraction observed
- **14p8-0add-17deg**: 181.4 bar, 0.65 — clean, good balance
- **17-0add-13deg run2**: 354.4 bar, 0.61 — high modulus but coverage issues, high CV

### Validation Status

**14-0add-8deg** (polymer_wt=14, bath_temp=8, mixing_temp=30, pullcast_speed=5, N2=true, wait=120s, nips=1250s): **Only 1 synthesis run**. This is the highest pore fraction observed (0.75) with decent modulus (103.6 bar). It is a Pareto-front candidate with a large apparent gain in pore fraction — it needs independent validation before being treated as confirmed.

**17-0add-13deg** (polymer_wt=17, bath_temp=13, mixing_temp=25, pullcast_speed=15, N2=true, wait=100s, nips=1800s): 4 runs with highly variable results (modulus 260–354 bar, pore fraction 0.40–0.65). The run2 result (354 bar, 0.61) is the highest modulus+pore fraction combination but has high CV and coverage defects. The run1 result (260 bar, 0.65) is more reproducible-looking but only one clean run.

### Decision

The **14-0add-8deg** candidate (14 wt%, bath 8°C, mixing 30°C, speed 5 mm/s, N2, wait 120s, nips 1250s) is the clearest Pareto-front candidate requiring validation: it has the highest pore fraction (0.75) with moderate modulus (103.6 bar), good membrane quality (minor surface creases only), low CV (0.04), and has never been independently repeated. A large apparent gain in pore fraction from a single run warrants confirmation before treating it as a reliable operating point.

This repeat will:
1. Confirm whether pore fraction ~0.75 is reproducible at these conditions
2. Establish whether modulus ~103 bar is stable
3. Determine if this is a genuine Pareto improvement over the 14.8wt/17°C candidate (181 bar, 0.65)
